answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from a bonded-identity registry where every new agent identity must post a stake locked for a full epoch. Creating a thousand identities therefore means a thousand stakes held hostage at once, which bleeds an attacker dry long before the horizon of the attack arrives. Honest agents earn back their stake plus fees, while anyone flooding the ledger with clones faces a gale of collateral they cannot recycle fast. Each identity also carries a pigment of provable history, signed work and peer attestations, that copies cannot forge.
